facts.assertion: Planning Data coordinate queries use latitude and longitude to return entities whose geometry intersects the supplied point.
Planning Data allows multiple dataset parameters in one coordinate query and returns entities from any requested dataset whose geometry covers the point.
Planning Data explicitly warns that absence of query results does not mean no constraints exist because data coverage varies by area.
Planning Data documentation identifies Lambeth local planning authority entity ID 626195 as an example for spatial filtering.
The documented Brownfield-area pattern uses geometry_entity with geometry_relation=within rather than point proximity.
Planning Data states that its planning-applications specification is currently in development and local authorities are not yet required to share application data to that specification.
Custom spatial geometry queries in Planning Data use WGS84 / EPSG:4326 coordinates.
Planning Data paginates large entity searches with limit and offset parameters.
Planning Data responses include pre-built next, prev, first and last pagination links.
Planning Data documents that the API does not provide a batch endpoint for property-by-property screening.
For hundreds of properties or more, Planning Data recommends bulk downloads and local spatial intersections to avoid rate limits and obtain a stable snapshot.
Planning Data bulk downloads are available in CSV, JSON and, where applicable, GeoJSON and Parquet.
The Planning Data API requires longitude and latitude together for point-intersection searches.
Planning Data exposes geometry relations including within, equals, disjoint, intersects, touches, contains, covers, coveredby, overlaps and crosses.
Planning Data provides a dedicated get-entity endpoint /entity/{entity}.{extension} for a known entity ID.
Planning Data describes its API as beta and warns that production integrations may need to accommodate changes.
